Uma Shankar @ Munnu vs Ajab Singh Narwariya on 7 April,
2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Gwl:8045
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Gwalior
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Ashish Shroti
 On The 7 th Of April, 2025
 Misc. Appeal No. 138 of 2013
 Uma Shankar @ Munnu
 Versus
 Ajab Singh Narwariya And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri R.P.Gupta - Advocate for the appellant.
 Shri Arvind Kumar Agrawal- Advocate for respondent No.
 3/Insurance Company.
 Order

Appellant/claimant has filed this appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 challenging the award dated 20/10/2012 passed by First Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bhind in Claim Case No. 28/2012.

entities.text: First Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bhind
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Pursuant to the accident met by the claimant with a Commander Jeep bearing registration No. UP-75-A-1707 (hereinafter shall be referred to as "offending vehicle"), the claimant filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation on account of the injuries suffered by him and vide impugned award,
learned Claims Tribunal awarded a compensation of Rs. 52,000/- to the claimant for the injuries suffered by him in road accident dated 3/6/2009.

2. It is not in dispute that the offending vehicles was owned by respondent No. 2 and was driven by respondent No. 1, while it was insured NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:8045 2 MA-138-2013 with respondent No. 3/Insurance Company.
It is also unchallenged finding of the Claims Tribunal that the appellant suffered injuries in tibia and fibula bones of right leg.

After the evidence led by both the sides, the Claims Tribunal has awarded Rs. 38,000/- towards actual expenses incurred by the claimant and a consolidated sum of Rs. 52,000/- has been awarded including the compensation on account of loss of income, pain and suffering.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the Tribunal has erred in not believing the disability certified (Ex. P/65), wherein, the Medical Board assessed the permanent disability to the extent of 40% suffered by the appellant.
He submits that the compensation ought to have been determined taking into account the permanent disability certified.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company submitted that even though the disability certificate was filed on record and exhibited by the claimant, it was not proved by examining any doctor, therefore, in absence of examination of any doctor, Claims Tribunal was justified in not believing the disability certified.

5. Considered the arguments and perused the record.
6.
It is an admitted fact in this case that no doctor has been examined in order to prove the medical certificate exhibited as Ex. P/65.

The submission of learned counsel for the appellant is that it was a certificate issued by the Medical Board and therefore ought to have been accepted by the Tribunal even in absence of statement of any of the doctors.

7. This issue has been considered by the Apex Court in the case of Rajkumar Vs. Ajay Kuamr and Anr., 2011 ACJ 1, wherein the Apex Court NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:8045 3 MA-138-2013 in para 7 held as under:-
"7.The percentage of permanent disability is expressed by the Doctors with reference to the whole body, or more often than not, with reference to a particular limb.

entities.text: Rajkumar Vs. Ajay Kuamr and Anr., 2011 ACJ 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: When a disability certificate states that the injured has suffered permanent disability to an extent of 45% of the left lower limb, it is not the same as 45% permanent disability with reference to the whole body.

The extent of disability of a limb (or part of the body) expressed in terms of a percentage of the total functions of that limb, obviously cannot be assumed to be the extent of disability of the whole body.

If there is 60%
permanent disability of the right hand and 80% permanent disability of left leg, it does not mean that the extent of permanent disability with reference to the whole body is 140% (that is 80% plus 60%).

If different parts of the body have suffered different. percentages of disabilities, the sum total thereof expressed in terms of the permanent disability with reference to the whole body, cannot obviously exceed 100%."

8. Again the issue came up for consideration before this Court in the case of Nathulal Vs. Kachrulal and Ors., 2014 ACJ 263 , wherein, in para 7, this Court has held as under:-
"7. Now coming to the point of enhancement, it is seen from the record that certificate of permanent disability, Exh. P68, had been produced but the doctor has not proved it stating the fact that it is signed by him and his signature has been put thereupon.

entities.text: Nathulal Vs. Kachrulal and Ors., 2014 ACJ 263
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Mr. Manish Jain, learned counsel for the appellant, contends that the contents of the said certificate have been stated by the doctor, however, it should be relied upon.

In the considered opinion of this court, until and unless the doctor issuing certificate has proved it by proving his signature on certificate, it cannot be relied upon and, therefore, the Tribunal has not committed any error in disbelieving the certificate of permanent disability.
In such circumstances, the finding of not accepting the plea of disability appears to be just and proper.

It is further seen from the record that injured has suffered compound fracture of tibia fibula bone and while Uma Shankar @ Munnu vs Ajab Singh Narwariya on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90364215/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
awarding compensation the Tribunal has not granted any amount of compensation under the head of grievous injures, however, in the facts and circumstances of the case and looking to the treatment and other papers available on record,
compensation of Rs. 40,000/- in lump sum in addition to the compensation NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:8045 4 MA-138-2013 already awarded by the Claims Tribunal deserves to be awarded for compound fracture of tibia fibula bone."

9. In view of annunciation of law by the Apex Court as also by this Court, it is settled that in absence of examination of doctor, that the disability certificate could not have been relied upon by the Claims Tribunal, the findings of Tribunal in this regard is therefore, held to be legal and valid and the same is hereby upheld.

10. Learned counsel for the appellant then relied upon the guidelines / instructions issued by M.P.
State Legal Services Authority prescribing the amount of compensation that may be awarded in absence of disability certificate in respect of grievous injury.
In respect of fracture of both tibia and fibula, a consolidated compensation of Rs. 60,000/- is payable to the claimant.
In addition to the same, the hospitalization charges @ Rs. 750/- per day is to be paid.
There is nothing on record to prove the hospitalization of claimant.
Thus, no amount can be awarded under this head.

11.Thus, relying upon the guidelines issued by the M.P. State Legal Services Authority, the appellant is held to get Rs. 60,000/- as compensation in respect of injuries suffered by him in addition to the amount of Rs. 38,000/- which has already been awarded by the Tribunal towards actual expenses.

Under such circumstances, appellant is held entitled to receive a total compensation of Rs.
98,000/-.
12.
The Claims Tribunal has already awarded a compensation of Rs. 52,000/- to the appellant

,
therefore, the compensation is enhanced by Rs. 46,000/- which is payable alongwith interest @ 6%
per annum from the date of application filed before the Claims Tribunal i.e. 22/07/2010.
Rest of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:8045 5 MA-138-2013 conditions as imposed by the Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.
13. The appeal is allowed in part in the aforesaid terms.

(ASHISH SHROTI) JUDGE JPS/-
